newsitem.title: CHINA: China gold, copper, lead mining capacities down.
newsitem.headline: China gold, copper, lead mining capacities down.

text.p: China's gold, copper, lead and zinc mining capacity has been falling because many state mines are nearly exhausted, the Economic Information Daily said on Tuesday.
A group of large and medium-sized state mines that have been in operation since the 1950s or 1960s are almost exhausted, the newspaper said. It did not identify the mines.
Production costs of the mines had soared because mining had become more difficult, it said.
Flagging investment also contributed to shrinking mining capacity, the newspaper said, adding that China would try to attract more foreign investment.
China's gold mining capacity was forecast to plummet by 70 percent by the year 2000, the newspaper said.
It did not give the current mining capacity. China produced 120.6 tonnes of gold in 1996, up from 108 tonnes in 1995.
Copper mining capacity was expected to decrease 26 percent by the end of the century, while lead and zinc mining capacity was expected to plunge 40 percent, the newspaper said.
Coal and iron mining capacity was forecast to slip 10 percent by 2000, the newspaper said.
